text: {"reply": "Thank you for being upfront, Dean. I checked your Lumen's warranty. The basic coverage (3 years / 60,000 km) and the powertrain coverage (5 years / 100,000 km) are both past their limits. The corrosion coverage is still active, but it excludes stone chips. A crack that began as a stone chip is impact damage, so I can't treat it as a manufacturing defect. Many insurance policies have a glass claim option, and that may be the quickest route. I'm also passing your file to a colleague, who can arrange an inspection of the windscreen and review your case.", "action": "escalated", "escalation_reason": "policy_limit", "summary": "Customer Dean Brown (verified with last name and plate CBFR 790) has a 2022 Meridian Lumen at 104,315 km. He asks for a long windscreen crack to be treated as a manufacturing defect. He says it started as a stone chip a few months ago. Basic and powertrain warranty are out of limits. Corrosion is in force but excludes stone chips. No claim draft was sent. I told him the crack is impact damage, so I can't call it a defect, and I mentioned insurance. A person should offer an inspection and a documented review if he wants one.", "policy_rules_cited": ["P-03", "P-04", "P-08", "P-09"]}
